label: substantive_advice_citing_statute
post_title: Released under investigation after drug driving - what next?

input.text:
Your sample will be sent for testing. In approximately 4-5 months the police will get the result back, if you exceed one or more of the 17 specified limits under Section 5A of the Road Traffic Act you'll be charged and given a court date by letter or phone call. That's usually the point you'll want to hire a solicitor before your plea hearing to enter a guilty/not guilty plea. Some people hire a solicitor before the result is back, but if you turn out to be under the limit you would usually end up having wasted some money. 

The minimum ban is 12 months if you're found guilty and there will be a fine which is discounted for an early guilty plea.

Alternatively, if you are below the limit and the police have evidence that you were impaired at the time you were driving you could be charged with Section 4 of the Road Traffic Act, the process would be similar. You could be charged with both if you are over a limit and there was evidence of impairment.

label: corrective_reply_clarifying_mens_rea_under_named_statute
post_title: Will I be prosecuted for wasting emergency services time? England

input.text:
It's an offence to **knowingly** give a false alarm of fire to the fire service, under [section 49 of the Fire and Rescue Services Act 2004](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/21/section/49).

There are two elements to this offence:

* the alarm must be false; and

* you must **know** that the alarm is false

In this case, it turned out the alarm was false.  But you didn't know the alarm was false - you didn't know whether the alarm was true or not.  That's not good enough for this offence - you must actually know that the alarm is false at the time you give it, otherwise the offence is incomplete.

label: procedural_reminder_notice_period_and_regulator_referral
post_title: [England] Each time I have self isolated due to covid, work have put it down as my holiday allowance, rather than sick.

input.text:
>Have i been mugged off here 

Yep. For your employer to enforce annual leave, they need to provide at least twice the notice than the leave they're enforcing. So if they had you off on annual leave for 10 days, they should've provided 20 days notice. 

They could have asked whether you wanted to use AL while isolating. But it should have been SSP at minimum (so long as you qualify for it - earn £120 a week more, are an employee etc) 

> and do i have any powers to claim this back? 

Eventually, possibly. You may want to raise it with the employer in the first instance to allow them to resolve it. This could be done via a grievance if necessary. 

Contact [ACAS](http://acas.org.uk) to find out more regarding potentially challenging the employer externally if the internal steps fail.
